input: Draft a reading curriculum for my homeschool co-op

keyUnknowns.whyItMatters: Reading curricula can range from pure phonics and decoding to comprehension, literary analysis, vocabulary, and writing response — knowing what is included or excluded shapes the entire structure.
The age or grade range of the students fundamentally changes the content, complexity, and skill targets of every part of the curriculum.
How often and for how long the co-op meets determines how many lessons to plan and how much can realistically be covered.
The time span the curriculum needs to cover (one semester, one year, etc.) sets the total volume of content and pacing requirements.
Whether the curriculum relies on a specific existing program, self-sourced texts, or must be built from scratch affects what resources need to be listed or created.
Co-ops often have a philosophical or pedagogical lean (classical, Charlotte Mason, secular, faith-based, literature-led, etc.) that should drive book selection and instructional style.

Knowing what the curriculum is meant to produce — a lesson-by-lesson plan, a booklist with discussion guides, a scope-and-sequence document, etc. — determines the format and depth of the final output.

gold.taskTitle: Draft a reading curriculum for homeschool co-op
gold.taskDescription: Create a structured reading curriculum tailored for use in a homeschool co-op setting.

questions.title: What grade or age range are the students?
questions.description: Identify the specific grade levels or ages of the co-op students this curriculum is designed for.

questions.title: Which reading skills should the curriculum cover?
questions.description: Clarify whether the focus is phonics, fluency, comprehension, literary analysis, vocabulary, written response, or some combination.

questions.title: How long should the curriculum span — one semester or a full year?
questions.description: Determine the total duration the curriculum needs to cover to set pacing and volume of content.

questions.title: How often does your co-op meet, and for how long each session?
questions.description: Understand the meeting frequency and session length to plan the number of lessons and realistic lesson depth.

questions.title: Does the co-op follow a specific educational philosophy or approach?
questions.description: Identify any philosophical or pedagogical orientation — classical, Charlotte Mason, secular, faith-based, etc. — that should shape book choices and teaching style.

questions.title: Should the curriculum use specific books or be built from scratch?
questions.description: Determine whether there are existing texts, programs, or book lists to incorporate, or whether all materials need to be sourced and created fresh.

questions.title: What does the finished curriculum document need to include?
questions.description: Clarify the expected output format — a scope-and-sequence, week-by-week lesson plans, a booklist with discussion guides, or another deliverable.
